newsitem.title: GERMANY: No sales boost for German stores from longer hours.
newsitem.headline: No sales boost for German stores from longer hours.

text.p: The extension of shop hours last November has brought little relief to German store owners and retail sales will stagnate in 1997 for the fifth year in a row, the country's HDE retail federation said on Thursday.
The HDE said that, above all, small retailers had lost out because they had failed to recapture the extra costs of staying open late by pulling in extra turnover.
Even though half of stores employing up to five staff had made use of new rules letting them open to 8 p.m. on weekdays and 4 p.m. on Saturdays, only 11 percent reported higher sales.

Of stores employing over 100 workers, however, 37 percent said their sales rose from November through to February against a year earlier. But nearly two-thirds of larger stores suffered stagnant or falling turnover, the HDE said.
"Considering the generous extension to store hours that is an unsatisfactory result," the HDE said. Four-fifths of stores are staying open at least five extra hours a week.

The HDE said it expected retail sales to grow by a nominal rate of 0.5 to one percent this year, which would equate to stagnation in real terms. Record post-war unemployment is to blame for consumer caution, the organisation added.
Retail turnover rose by a nominal 0.7 percent last year to 920 billion marks, which worked out as a 0.2 percent fall adjusted to take account for inflation.

Despite the gloomy view given by the HDE, a market research group on Thursday gave a more upbeat view on consumer confidence. The GfK research firm said that, although consumer confidence fell in February by 3.2 percent from January, it was still 10 percent up on a year earlier.
GfK said increasing readiness to buy may represent a catchup to years of restraint, and added government plans to raise value-added tax could prompt a new spurt in retail sales.
The GfK consumer confidence indicator is based on a question to a representative sample of 2,500 consumers on whether they think it wise at the moment to buy more.
